players.product: Power and distribution transformers and substations (T&D) for grid connection, plus Marathon alternators for data-center energy backup and industrial pumps / ventilation equipment for cooling systems

quarterly_data.signal: WEG announced a US$ 165 million (approximately BRL 840 million) investment plan to expand generator production capacity in North America, in two phases, aimed at power generation for critical applications in the U.S., 'particularly driven by the expansion of data centers' (businesses acquired with Marathon). Phase one: US$ 24 million to acquire and adapt an industrial building next to the Quma I Industrial Park in Atotonilco de Tula, Mexico, for generator assembly, with operations expected to begin in the second quarter of 2027. Phase two: US$ 141 million for two new vertically integrated industrial facilities (laminations, low- and medium-voltage windings, shafts and frames) at a North American location yet to be defined. On completion of the second phase, scheduled for 2030, WEG will be able to manufacture approximately 50 generators per day globally at its facilities in Mexico, the U.S., Brazil and China, versus a current capacity of 10 generators per day.
quarterly_data.figure: US$ 165 million; generator capacity approximately 50 per day by 2030 (currently 10 per day); phase one operations Q2 2027
